speaker: Bernd Siebert
title: Intrinsic mirror symmetry
abstract: In the talk I will sketch the completion of the joint project with Mark Gross on the intrinsic construction of mirror families for pairs $(X,D)$ and their degenerations, assuming only $K_X$ nef or $(X,D)$ log Calabi-Yau, as announced in our survey with the same title from 2016. The construction is based on the notion of punctured Gromov-Witten invariants under development in parallel jointly with Dan Abramovich and Qile Chen.

speaker: Yijia Liu
title: On pseudo-Anosov autoequivalences II
abstract: In this talk, we propose a new definition of pseudo-Anosov autoequivalences, which turns out to be more general than the one proposed by Dimitrov-Haiden-Katzarkov-Kontsevich. We construct new examples of pseudo-Anosov autoequivalences on quintic Calabi-Yau threefolds and quiver Calabi-Yau categories. We prove that they act hyperbolically on the space of Bridgeland stability conditions for the quiver examples. This is a joint work in progress with Fan, Filip, and Katzarkov.

speaker: Ben Webster
title: Tilting bundles and 3-dimensional field theory
abstract: The category of coherent sheaves on an interesting variety $X$ has an extremely annoying property: does not have enough projectives, so it cannot be equivalent to the category of modules over an algebra. However, if you pass to the derived category, this defect can be fixed in many interesting cases, by finding a tilting generator: that is, a vector bundle $T$ such that any coherent sheaf can be resolved by a complex consisting of sums of copies of $T$, and $Ext^i(T,T)=0$ for all i>0. If $A=End(T)$, then we obtain an equivalence of derived categories between finitely generated $A$-modules and $Coh(X)$. This provides a bridge between representation theory and algebraic geometry. This bridge was largely built for us by Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin, but they did not make it very easy for the rest of us to cross it; in particular, while both ends of the bridge are in characteristic 0, the middle is in characteristic p. I’ll talk about how recent input from work in 3d field theory by Braverman, Finkelberg and Nakajima allows us in certain cases to reroute this bridge and avoid characteristic p, while getting a more concrete understanding of the algebra A on the other side.

title: On pseudo-Anosov autoequivalences

speaker: Ilia Zharkov
title: Equal rights: the case of pair-of-pants.
abstract: In addition to the usual complex pair-of-pants and phase tropical pair-of-pants I will propose two other spaces, all four being homeomorphic to each other. In the first (amplitude pair-of-pants) the amoeba plays the role of the coamoeba and vice versa. In the second both are treated equally giving an altimate ''ober tropical" space which looks like cotangent space to the skeleton, a symplectic geometer dream.

speaker: Lino Amorim
title: Gromov-Witten invariants for Calabi-Yau categories II
abstract: I will discuss how to define genus zero Gromov-Witten invariants for $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded Calabi-Yau $A_\infty$-categories with semi-simple Hochschild cohomology. These categorical invariants depend on the choice of a grading operator on the Hochschild homology. In the case of the Fukaya category of a symplectic manifold it is expected that, for the appropriate choice of grading, these categorical invariants match the geometric ones. I will show this is the case for projective spaces.

title: Gromov-Witten invariants for Calabi-Yau categories

speaker: Nikita Nekrasov
affiliation: Simons Center for Geometry and Physics
title: Magnificent Four with Colors.
abstract: We study the rank N magnificent four theory, which is the supersymmetric localization of U(N) super-Yang-Mills theory with matter (a super-group U(N|N) gauge theory) on a Calabi-Yau fourfold. Our theory contains the higher rank Donaldson-Thomas theory of threefolds. We conjecture an explicit formula for the partition function Z, and report on the performed checks. The partition function Z has a free field representation. Surprisingly, it depends on the Coulomb and mass parameters in a simple way. We also clarify the definition of the instanton measure.

speaker: Ilia Zharkov
title: Improving topological SYZ fibrations: discriminant of codimension 2, continued.
abstract: In all known constructions of the torus fibrations of Calabi-Yau manifolds the discriminant locus on the base is of codimension 1 (except the trivial case of K3 and an Inventiones paper by Mark Gross for quintic threefold). In a joint project (in progress) with Helge Ruddat we try to show how to make it of codimension 2 for a very large class of examples.

speaker: Tudor Dimofte
title: Categories of line operators in 3d N=4 gauge theories.
abstract: A 3d N=4 gauge theory is labelled by a compact group G and a quaternionic representation R. Such physical theories also admit two distinct "A" and "B" topological twists, each of which gives rise to many layers of algebraic and geometric structures. I will review some of what's known and expected about these twists, and then discuss a proposed mathematical definition of one particular layer of structure: the (braided, monoidal) categories of line operators. The categories of line operators provide a generalization of the recent Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima construction of Coulomb branches, play an important role in symplectic duality, and have direct applications to the construction of HOMFLY link homologies.

speaker: Ilia Zharkov
title: Improving topological SYZ fibrations: discriminant of codimension 2
abstract: In all known constructions of the torus fibrations of Calabi-Yau manifolds the discriminant locus on the base is of codimension 1 (except the trivial case of K3 and an Inventiones paper by Mark Gross for quintic threefold). speaker: Matthew Ballard
title: Exceptional collections on arithmetic varieties.
abstract: The simplest way to capture the derived category of coherent sheaves on an algebraic variety is via an exceptional collection. In this talk, we will turn our attention to varieties over general fields and describe a Galois descent result for full exceptional collections. We will use arithmetic toric varieties as source of examples and questions. Hopefully the audience will provide the A-side version of the story. This talk is based on joint with work with A. Duncan and P. McFaddin.

speaker: Helge Ruddat
title: Periods integrals from wall structures.
abstract: Gluing a variety X from open subsets of algebraic tori along wall crossing automorphisms is a widespread technique for producing Calabi-Yau and Fano manifolds as well as cluster varieties, especially in the context of mirror symmetry. In joint work with Bernd Siebert, I provide an explicit computation of period integrals on X. The cycles to integrate come from tropical 1-cycles in an affine manifold that governs the gluing. Most interestingly, the period integrals turn out to be monomial functions in the parameters that determine the wall crossing. This leads to a proof of that the formal canonical proper Calabi-Yau families constructed by Gross and Siebert are completions of analytic families. In the K3 case, these periods can be used to determine which cohomology classes are algebraic.

speaker: Rina Anno
title: $\mathbb{P}$-twists and where to find them
abstract: For a $\mathbb{P}^n$-functor F between two categories, we can construct a $\mathbb{P}$-twist, which is an autoequivalence of the target category. I will go over the definition of a $\mathbb{P}$-twist, and give some algebro-geometric examples.

speaker: Sheel Ganatra
title: Structural results for wrapped Fukaya categories
abstract: I will describe a series of new structural results for (partially) wrapped Fukaya categories, including functoriality, generation results, a Kunneth embedding, “stop removal”/localization, and gluing. Using some these results, I will sketch a proof that the partially wrapped Fukaya category of a cotangent bundle coincides with (compact objects of) the relevant category of “large” microlocal sheaves on the zero section. This is joint work with J. Pardon and V. Shende.

speaker: Rina Anno
title: $\mathbb{P}^n$-functors and $\mathbb{P}^n$-twists
abstract: A functor between two triangulated categories is called a $\mathbb{P}^n$-functor if there exists certain additional data that we call a $\mathbb{P}^n$-structure. Having a functor with a $\mathbb{P}^n$-structure one can construct an autoequivalence of the target category called a $\mathbb{P}^n$-twist. I am going to introduce several versions of the definition of a $\mathbb{P}^n$-structure and discuss the possibility of finding a canonical form for it.

speaker: Yan Soibelman
title: Deformation quantization and Fukaya categories.
abstract: I am going to discuss the relation between deformation quantization and Fukaya categories in the framework of complex algebraic varieties.

speaker: Yan Soibelman
title: Fukaya category with singular Lagrangians
abstract:
In the conventional approach to Fukaya categories objects are supported on Lagrangian submanifolds, i.e. the supports are smooth. This is not enough for many reasons. For example, the Lagrangian skeleton of an exact symplectic manifold is typically singular. Furthermore, the union of two smooth Lagrangian subvarieties can be non-smooth. This affects the functoriality of construction.
In this talk I am going to outline a recent approach to the solution of the problem proposed by Kontsevich and myself.

speaker: Vivek Shende
title: User's guide to the wrapped Fukaya category II
abstract: I will describe some tools for manipulating wrapped Fukaya categories without getting one's hands dirty with holomorphic disk calculations all the time.

speaker: Lino Amorim
title: Mirror symmetry for an orbifold sphere
abstract: In this talk, I will construct a Landau-Ginzburg mirror for a sphere with three orbifold points using the Lagrangian Floer theory of an immersed circle. I will then prove closed mirror symmetry for this space: more precisely I will define an isomorphism between the big quantum cohomology ring of the orbifold and the Jacobian ring of the mirror potential.

speaker: Jamie Peabody
title: The polytope associated to the GIT fan of a Mori Dream Space II
abstract: A Mori Dream Space is naturally a GIT quotient of an affine variety by an algebraic torus. Such a GIT quotient naturally carries a combinatorial structure called the GIT fan. I will present my approach to describing the GIT fan using secondary fans and tropical geometry. As a result of this approach, I show that this fan is the normal fan to an explicitly computable polytope.

speaker: Hansol Hong
title: Mirror construction via gluing of Lagrangian deformation spaces
abstract: Formal deformation theory of a given Lagrangian $L$ in a symplectic manifold $X$ studies deformation of $A$-infinity structures on its Floer complex. It produces a local chart in the mirror of $X$ consisting of solutions of the Maurer-Cartan equation for the deformation, which encodes crucial information about holomorphic disks bounding $L$. In this talk, I will first discuss various interesting features of this local construction, and explain a method to glue local charts from different Lagrangians via isomorphisms between Lagrangians in the Fukaya category.

speaker: David Ben-Zvi
title: Algebraic Geometry of Topological Field Theory
abstract: A commutative ring is gainfully understood as functions on a geometric object, the spectrum of the ring. Observables in quantum mechanics form a typically noncommutative ring, and are harder to capture with traditional geometry. However, observables in quantum field theory in space-time of dimension d > 1 - and especially in the simplified models provided by topological field theory - enjoy increasing commutativity, and thus are more amenable to a geometric description. I will describe some aspects of the notion of the “spectrum” of a topological field theory, inspired by the work of Kontsevich and Soibelman on mirror symmetry (d = 2), the Seiberg-Witten geometry of supersymmetric gauge theories (d = 3 and 4), and electric-magnetic/Langlands duality (d = 4). Based on joint work with Andy Neitzke and Sam Gunningham.

speaker: Qiang Wang
title: Splitting attractor flows and DT invariants in SU(3) Seiberg-Witten integrable systems
abstract: We will start by constructing wall crossing structures on the base of the complex integrable system, which produces an algorithm for computing the DT invariants by employing certain trees on its base given through the splitting attractor flows. We will review the notion of splitting attractor flow and illustrate its use by applying the algorithm to the Seiberg-Witten integrable systems for SU(2) and SU(3).

speaker: Qiang Wang
title: Wall Crossing Structures in Seiberg-Witten Integrable Systems.
abstract: Wall crossing structure (WCS) is a formalism that could be used to encode the Donaldson-Thomas invariants in mathematics. In this talk, we will review the notion of WCS and see how it can be induced from the data coming from a complex integrable system. In particularly, we will apply this formalism to the Seiberg-Witten integrable systems that are relevant for the N=2 super symmetric Yang-Mills theory for gauge groups SU(2) and SU(3), which would enable us to encode the known BPS spectrum of the theories.

speaker: Peter Koroteev
title: DAHA and Brane Quantization.
abstract: Double affine Hecke algebras (DAHA) arise in many places in mathematics and string theory. I. Cherdnik used DAHA to prove Macdonald conjectures while knot theorists constructed homological invariants of torus knots using this algebras. It was shown by Oblomkov that A-type DAHA arises as deformation quantization of the character variety of the once-punctured torus. I shall discuss geometric representation theory of DAHA using branes in 2d A model on the Hitchin moduli space M_H. We shall arrive to a conjecture that the category of A-branes on M_H is equivalent to a representation category of DAHA.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: Spheres in complex hypersurfaces II.
abstract: Given a hypersurface X of the complex torus, mirror symmetry predicts a quasi-equivalence between the Fukaya category F(X) of X and a certain category of graded matrix factorizations MF (W) on a toric Calabi-Yau variety. In this talk, I will describe this correspondence, as well as how it fits in the larger picture of homological mirror symmetry. Exploring the algebraic side, one finds there are many spherical objects in MF (W) which have combinatorial descriptions. Using phase tropical varieties, I will provide a prediction of the topological mirrors to these objects in F(X) and discuss some generalizations. This is based on joint work with Ilia Zharkov.

speaker: Timothy Logvinenko
title: Perverse schobers and orbifolds.
abstract: Perverse schobers are a recent notion introduced by Kapranov and Schechtman. It is a categorification of perverse sheaves on a stratified topological space. In this talk, I will discuss perverse sheaves and perverse schobers on an orbifold disc.

speaker: Yan Soibelman
title: Fukaya categories of complex symplectic surfaces and periodic monopoles.
abstract: I will explain why a parabolic version of the Fukaya category of the partially compactified symplectic surfaces of certain type should be related to the 3-dimensional dimensional reductions of the 4-dimensional autoduality equations.

speaker: Jamie Peabody
title: GIT fan for Mori Dream Space
abstract: Abstract: In this talk I will introduce the secondary fan of a marked polytope and the secondary fan of a closed subgroup of an algebraic torus acting on affine space. I will then use these constructions to describe how the unstable locus changes as we move between chambers in the secondary fan

speaker: Nikon Kurnosov
title: Generalized Kuga-Satake construction for hyperkahler manifolds
abstract: Abstract: The classic Kuga-Satake construction gives us a Hodge structure of weight one by K3-type Hodge structure. I will talk about joint work with A.Soldatenkov and M.Verbitsky, in which we generalize Kuga-Satake construction and embed cohomology of hyperk\"ahler manifolds to cohomology of some complex torus which is morphism of Hodge structures. I will discuss also some applications of this result.

speaker: Yu-Wei Fan
title: Systoles, Special Lagrangians, and Bridgeland stability conditions
abstract: Motivated by Loewner's torus inequality which relates the least length of a non-contractible loop (systole) on a torus to its volume, one can ask whether there is a higher-dimensional analogue, with torus replaced by Calabi-Yau manifolds and loops replaced by special Lagrangian submanifolds. We attempt to answer this question in the case of mirror quartic K3 surfaces via mirror symmetry and Bridgeland stability conditions. We define the notion of categorical systole and systolic ratio of a Bridgeland stability condition, and show that the aforementioned question is related to a purely lattice-theoretic problem. We prove that the answer to the lattice-theoretic problem is finite and give an explicit upper bound.

speaker: Junwu Tu
title: Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau categories
abstract: Classical mirror symmetry relates Gromov-Witten invariants in symplectic geometry to Yukawa coupling invariants in algebraic geometry. Through non-commutative Hodge theory, one can define categorical Gromov-Witten invariants associated to (Calabi-Yau A-infinity) categories. Conjecturally, this construction should reproduce the Gromov-Witten invariants and Yukawa coupling invariants, when applied Fukaya categories and Derived categories, respectively. In this talk, I describe a first computation of categorical Gromov-Witten invariants at positive genus. This is a joint work with Andrei Caldararu.

speaker: Ludmil Katzarkov
title: Categrical Brill Noether invariants.
abstract: Abstract: In this talk we will introduce some new categorical invariants. We connect them with some classical questions in combinatorics and geometry

speaker: Benjamin Gammage
title: Two perspectives on mirror symmetry for hypersurfaces
abstract: Abstract: Recent developments in the theory of microlocal sheaves allow us to compute symplectic invariants from the skeleton of a symplectic manifold. We will explain this in the context of affine hypersurfaces, for which we will describe two types of skeleta and derive proofs of homological mirror symmetry

speaker: Weiwei Wu
title: Spherical twists and projective twists in Fukaya categories
abstract: Seidel's Lagrangian Dehn twist exact sequence has been a cornerstone of the theory of Fukaya categories. In the last decade, Huybrechts and Thomas discovered a new autoequivalence in the derived cateogry of coherent sheaves using the so-called "projective objects", which are presumably mirrors of Lagrangian projective spaces. On the other hand, Seidel's construction of Lagrangian Dehn twists as symplectomorphisms can be easily generalized to Lagrangian projective spaces. The induce auto-equivalence on Fukaya categories are conjectured to be the mirror of Huybrechts-Thomas's auto-equivalence on B-side. This remains open until recently, and I will explain my joint work with Cheuk-Yu Mak on the solution to this conjecture using the technique of Lagrangian cobordisms. Moreover, we will explain a recent progress, again joint with Cheuk-Yu Mak, on pushing this further to Lagrangian embeddings of finite quotients of rank-one symmetric spaces, leading to another new class of auto-equivalences, which are different from the classical spherical twists only in coefficients of finite characteristics.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: Homological mirror symmetry of birational cobordisms II
abstract: Abstract: A birational cobordism is a basic variation of GIT from a stack $X_+$ to $X_-$. On the level of derived categories, this results in a semi-orthogonal decomposition $D(X_+) = \left< D(X_- ) , \mathcal{T} \right>$ where $\mathcal{T}$ has a full exceptional collection. There is a mirror to this basic operation which yields a homological mirror to $\mathcal{T}$. This is a Landau-Ginzburg model on a higher dimensional pair-of-pants. This talk will explain this result and sketch the proof of the one dimensional case. The general case follows from dimensional induction which will be explored if time permits.

speaker: Yan Soibelman
title: Algebraicity in wall-crossing formulas and cluster transformations I, II
abstract: It was observed by physicists and mathematicians that many generating series appearing in Donaldson-Thomas theory are in fact algebraic functions. In a joint project with Maxim Kontsevich we propose a general reason for that: algebraicity comes from the structure of the moduli space of certain rational curves in a non-archimedean space associated with stability data on a graded Lie algebra of vector fields on a torus. In my talks I am going to explain main ideas of our approach.

speaker: Roman Fedorov
title: Variations of Hodge structures for hypergeometric differential operators I, II
abstract: Consider the holomorphic bundle with connection on $$\mathbb{P}^1-\{0,1,\infty\}$$ corresponding to the regular hypergeometric differential operator \prod_{j=1}^h(D-\alpha_j)-z\prod_{j=1}^h(D-\beta_j),\qquad D=z\frac{d}{dz} Under certain assumptions on real numbers $$\alpha_j \hspace{1cm} \text{ and } \hspace{1cm}\beta_j,$$ this bundle is known to underlie a complex polarizable variation of Hodge structures. We calculate some Hodge invariants for this variation, in particular, the Hodge numbers. This is a generalization of a conjecture of Corti and Golyshev.

speaker: Emanuel Diaconescu
title: Donaldson-Thomas invariants and character varieties
abstract: A string theoretic framework will be presented relating the cohomology of character varieties with tame ramification to Donaldson-Thomas invariants of Calabi-Yau orbifolds. This construction yields a string theoretic derivation of a conjecture of Hausel, Letellier and Rodriguez-Vilegas, explaining the occurrence of Macdonald polynomials in this context. Based on work with W.-y. Chuang, R. Donagi and T. Pantev.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: Constructions in Floer theory I, II
abstract: Behind every good Fukaya category stands a robust Floer theoretic framework. Floer's equation and its TQFT perspective leads to several important constructions and results in mirror symmetry, symplectic geometry and dynamics. In this sequence of talks, I will review some of the most salient points of the theory, their motivation and applications.

speaker: Zack Sylvan
title: Gluing Fukaya categories
abstract: I will define partially wrapped Fukaya categories, which extend Fukaya-Seidel categories to general exact Landau-Ginzburg models. These categories satisfy a gluing formula, and using that I'll give a presentation for the wrapped Fukaya category of arbitrary punctured Riemann surfaces in terms of A_n quiver representations. This confirms that various combinatorial models agree with Floer theory. I'll also explain how to use gluing to prove generation results, and I'll discuss tentative connections to Lagrangian skeleta and contact homolog

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: Partially wrapped Fukaya categories associated to skeleta
abstract: I will briefly describe Fukaya categories and their wrapped and partially wrapped versions. The central technical obstacles associated to their definitions will be surveyed. I will then give examples of non-trivial, computable partially wrapped Fukaya categories associated to simplicial complexes. If time permits, applications to mirror symmetry will be discussed.

speaker: Yan Soibelman
title: Riemann-Hilbert correspondence and Fukaya categories
abstract: Riemann-Hilbert correspondence establishes categorical equivalence between D-modules and constructible sheaves. I am going to discuss how symplectic topology appears in the story.

speaker: Alexander Odesskii
title: Deformations of complex structures on Riemann surfaces and integrable structures of Whitham type hierarchies
abstract: We obtain variational formulas for holomorphic objects on Riemann surfaces with respect to arbitrary local coordinates on the moduli space of complex structures. These formulas are written in terms of a canonical object on the moduli space which corresponds to the pairing between the space of quadratic differentials and the tangent space to the moduli space. This canonical object satisfies certain commutation relations which appear to be the same as the ones that emerged in the integrability theory of Whitham type hierarchies. Driven by this observation, we develop the theory of Whitham type hierarchies integrable by hydrodynamic reductions as a theory of certain differential-geometric objects. As an application we prove that the universal Whitham hierarchy is integrable by hydrodynamic reductions

speaker: Nicolo Sibilla
title: Topological Fukaya category and homological mirror symmetry
abstract: The topological Fukaya category is a combinatorial model of the Fukaya category of exact symplectic manifolds which was first proposed by Kontsevich. In this talk I will explain work in progress (joint with J. Pascaleff and S. Scherotzke) on gluing techniques for the topological Fukaya category that are closely related to Viterbo functoriality. I will emphasize applications to homological mirror symmetry for three-dimensional CY LG models, and to Bondal's and Fang-Liu-Treumann-Zaslow's coherent constructible correspondence for toric varieties.

speaker: Sergey Arkhipov
title: Braid group actions on the categories of equivariant matrix factorizations
abstract: Let G be a reductive algebraic group with a chosen Borel subgroup B. Given an algebraic variety X with an action of the group G we define the category of equivariant matrix factorizations on the product of $T^*X$ with the Lie algebra of B. The potential is obtained from the moment map. We relate the defined category with the category of coherent sheaves on the Hamiltonian reduction of $T^*X$ with respect to B. Extending a consturction of Bezrukavnikov and Riche, we define a categorical action of the affine Braid group on the category of equivariant matrix factorizations. We reformulate the definition of affine Hecke category due to Bezrukavnikov and show that braid relations for the action above would follow from a certain conjecture in Algebraic Geometry. The conjecture concerns logarithmic differential forms on Bott-Samelson desingularizations of Schubert varieties. Time permitting, we discuss the directions towards the proof of the conjecture.

speaker: Ed Dewey
title: Characteristic classes of spectral covers
abstract: Diagonalizing matrices is important, so how about doing it in families? A "spectral cover" is what you get if you try to diagonalize a family of regular matrices (a.k.a. a regular Higgs bundle). They can be topologically interesting: for example, the data of a line bundle or of an étale cover can be encoded by a spectral cover. I will talk about defining characteristic classes of spectral covers, living in rational cohomology. This amounts to computing the cohomology ring of the stack of spectral covers, and expressing its generators in terms of Chern classes of certain natural vector bundle.

speaker: Ilia Zharkov
title: How to disprove the Hodge Conjecture
abstract: In the 70's Mumford proposed a potential counterexample to Hodge conjecture by abelian varieties of Weil type. I will describe an idea of Kontsevich how tropical geometry can be used to show that the Weil classes in such abelian varieties are not represented by algebraic cycles.

abstract: In the 70's Mumford proposed a potential counterexample to Hodge conjecture by abelian varieties of Weil type. I will describe an idea of Kontsevich how tropical geometry can be used to show that the Weil classes in such abelian varieties are not represented by algebraic cycles.

speaker: Ilia Itenberg
title: Rational quintics in the real projective plane
abstract: The talk is devoted to an isotopy classification of nodal rational curves of degree 5 in the real projective plane. This is a joint work with Grigory Mikhalkin and Johannes Rau.

speaker: Yanki Lekili
title: Koszul duality in Floer theory.
abstract: We study symplectic invariants of the open symplectic manifolds X obtained by plumbing cotangent bundles of spheres according to a plumbing tree. We prove that certain models for the Fukaya category F(X) of closed exact Lagrangians in X and the wrapped Fukaya category W(X) are related by Koszul duality. As an application, we give explicit computations of symplectic cohomology, essentially for all trees. This is joint work with Tolga Etg\"u.

speaker: Yan Soibelman
title: Morse Theory, A-infinity categories and Mirror Symmetry II
abstract: I will start with the old work of Fukaya, in which he extended Morse theory beyond an additive isomorphism of cohomology groups. I will explain how those ideas were used in our old work with Kontsevich on Homological Mirror Symmetry for torus fibration. After discussing all those preliminaries I plan to move on to more recent developments, namely to the relationship of Morse theory and A-infinity categories in the framework of Landau-Ginzburg models suggested in a recent paper by Gaiotto-Moore-Witten. Among several applications of their approach I am going to discuss the old work of Kapranov and Saito on Morse theory and Stasheff polytopes.

speaker: David Treumann
title: Legendrian knots and constructible sheaves
abstract: I will discuss a "categorical" invariant of Legendrian knots -- to each such knot or link is attached a triangulated category which can be computed combinatorially. The category is equivalent to the Nadler-Zaslow version of the Fukaya category of Lagrangian surfaces that end on the knot. I will discuss some relations with (1) the Chekanov-Eliashberg theory of augmentations, (2) triply graded link homology (HOMFLY homology) and (3) algebraic plane curve singularities. The talk is based on joint work with Vivek Shende and Eric Zaslow.

speaker: Mikhail Movshev
title: On regularized geometry of loop spaces
abstract: It is safe to say that for a mathematician Quantum Mechanics means a spectral theory of elliptic PDE on a finite dimensional manifold. Physicists have to deal with quantum theories which formally do not fall into jurisdiction of finite-dimensional analysis. In particular the sigma-model Schradinger operator has to be defined on the free loop space $LM$ of a Riemannian manifold M. Roughly speaking the regularized loop space $L_NM$ has loops whose Fourier coefficients are nonzero only up to degree $N$. In the talk I will discuss topological and geometric properties of $L_NM$ when $M$ is a round sphere $S^k$ relevant to spectral theory on $L_NS^k$

speaker: Mikhail Mazin
title: Geometric Theory of Parshin Residues IV
abstract: Parshin residues is a multidimensional generalization of the classical residues of 1-forms on curves. Given an algebraic variety and a top meromorphic form on it, one can compute Parshin residues of the form. An important difference in higher dimensions is that one computes residues not at a point, but at a complete flag of subvarieties. Note that the subvarieties are allowed to be singular. The residues satisfy certain relations, called Parshin's Reciprocity Laws. The original Parshin's theory is very algebraic, applicable well beyond the case of complex coefficients. However, in the complex variable case one would expect a more geometric approach possible. We use the stratification theory to express Parshin residues in terms of integrals over smooth cycles. The Reciprocity Laws then follow from homological relations on these cycles. We also use resolution of singularities techniques to reduce the general situation to the case when all varieties are smooth and the divisor of poles of the differential form is a normal crossing divisor. The Reciprocity Laws are then replaced by the total sums of residues over certain compact curves.

speaker: Yan Soibelman
title: Fukaya-Seidel category in infrared limit I - VI
abstract: I am going to discuss our recent work with Kapranov and Kontsevich. It is motivated by the big unfinished paper by Gaiotto, Moore and Witten devoted to certain two-dimensional supersymmetric gauge theories, including Landau-Ginzburg model. Mathematically, it gives an alternative description of what is known as Fukaya-Seidel category for a Kahler manifold endowed with a holomorphic function (potential). Our description is based on the Morse theory of the real part of the potential as well as on some concepts of toric geometry (secondary polytopes). I plan to discuss some applications,including those to the Morse theory of non-Morse functions,higher-dimensional TFTs, wall-crossing formulas, etc.

speaker: Tom Mainiero
title: This one weird trick has algebraic functions generating Donaldson-Thomas invariants from home! Sit in this talk to see why!
abstract: It is a result of Kontsevich that generating functions for Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants associated to the m-Kronecker quiver are algebraic functions over the rationals. Using a technique from supersymmetric physics-- "spectral networks" -- one can see algebraicity of such functions directly and construct the associated algebraic equations in an algorithmic manner. We will discuss some interesting corollaries of these algebraic equations-- namely asymptotics on DT-invariants and Euler-characteristics of (Kronecker) quiver moduli-- and (if time allows) give a brief overview of the spectral network technique.

speaker: Sergey Cherkis
title: Hyperkaehler Spaces from Monopole Walls
abstract: Hyperkaehler metrics of real dimension four deliver simplest nontrivial examples of Calabi-Yau spaces. A rich source for such metrics is the self-dual Yang-Mills and its various reductions, such as the monopole equation, the Hitchin system, and the Nahm equations. After a short review of known metrics we focus on those with the lowest volume growth. These appear as moduli spaces of monopoles; to be exact, of doubly periodic monopoles. We call these monopole walls or monowalls. We compute the dimensions of the monowall moduli spaces, find nontrivial isometries between them, and find their asymptotic metrics explicitly. Spectral curves, their amoebas, Newton polygons, and their secondary polyhedrons play central role in this story. The leading behavior of the Kaehler potential, for example, is related to the volume of the melted crystal, i.e. the regularized volume under the Ronkin function of an associated spectral curve. We also explore the parameter space of such metrics and find its complete description in terms of fibered polytopes and secondary fans.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: The homological mirror to the punctured plane
abstract: Symplectic mirrors to algebraic varieties are known in many instances. For example, Calabi-Yau varieties, Fano varieties and open Calabi-Yaus. When the variety is quasi-affine, little is known and less is proven. I will speak about a work in progress with Katzarkov and Kontsevich that describes a Fukaya category mirror to the punctured plane, and more generally, to any affine, quasi-affine and projective toric stack.

speaker: Dima Arinkin
title: Singular support of coherent sheaves and the geometric Langlands program
abstract:
In its `categorical' version, the geometric Langlands conjecture predicts deep ties between quasi-coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local systems and D-modules on the moduli stack of principal bundles. It is very natural to state the conjecture as an equivalence between the derived categories of these objects. However, such naive formulation turns out to be inconsistent: the two categories do not match. In a joint work with D. Gaitsgory, we develop a way to correct this issue using the notion of singular support of coherent sheaves. Roughly speaking, to get an equivalence of categories, quasicoherent sheaves should be replaced with (ind)coherent sheaves whose singular support is contained in a certain natural subset. In this talk, I will show how singular support of coherent sheaves allows one to `correct' the categorical Langlands conjecture so that it passes natural compatibility tests (such as compatibility with the Eisenstein series)

speaker: Alexei Oblomkov
title: The elliptic Affine Springer Fibers in type Cherednik Algebras and homological knot invariants
abstract: (Joint work with Zhiwei Yun) The Affine Springer Fibers from the title are homeomorphic to the compactified Jacobians $JC_{m,n}$ of curves ${x^m=y^n, (m,n)=1.}$ In elementary terms $JC_{m,n}$ is the space of subspaces $\subset \CC[[t]]$ of codimension $(m-1)(n-1)$ that are preserved by multiplication on $t^m$ and $t^n$. Together with Zhiwei Yun we described an action of the spherical rational Cherednik algebra $eH_{m/n}(S_n)e$ on $H^*(JC_{m,n})$ and the ring structure of the cohomology. The ring structure is very similar to the ring structure of the finite dimensional Grassmanians, and in my talk I will discuss this analogy and connections with q,t Catalan numbers and the Khovanov-Rozansky invariants of the torus knots. Talk is accessible to students familiar with basic topology and representation theory.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: Minimal model sequences and their mirrors I
abstract: In the first lecture, I will give a description of the toric minimal model program and classify all possible "straight line" runs. The classification can be given geometrically as vertices of an iterated fiber polytope (or as the fixed points of a particular toric stack). I will illustrate this polytope in certain cases and detail the relationship with the Mori and Sarkisov programs.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: Minimal model sequences and their mirrors II
abstract: In the second talk I will start fresh with several examples of DM toric stacks and their Mori theory. I will detail the combinatorial description of crossing a wall from one Mori chamber to another and describe the effect of such a wall crossing on the derived category of coherent sheaves. This talk will be independent of the first talk.

speaker: Mikhail Mazin
title: Local Hilbert Schemes and Jacobi Factors of Plane Curve Singularities
abstract: In this talk I will describe two invariants of a plane curve singularity: local Hilbert scheme and the Jacobi factor, and explain how they are related. Local Hilbert scheme is the moduli space of ideals in the complete local ring R of the singularity. The Jacobi factor is the moduli space of R-submodules in the normalization of R. I will mostly concentrate on the case of quasi-homogeneous unibranched singularities {x^m=y^n} with relatively prime positive $m$ and $n.$ In this case both the local Hilbert scheme and the Jacobi factor have affine cell decompositions with interesting and non-trivial combinatorics.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: The homological mirror of a toric stack
abstract: In this talk I will define the Hori-Vafa mirror LG potential of a toric stack. The homological version of this mirror is a directed Fukaya category. I will define this category and explain some of its basic properties. I will conclude with the description of the homological mirrors of the projective line and the projective plane.

speaker: Gabriel Kerr
title: Minimal model runs and degenerations
abstract: In this final talk I will explain several precise ways to degenerate a homological mirror LG model of X (in fact, a moduli of degenerations). For each such (maximal) degeneration, there is a mirror minimal model run of X. I will describe how to decompose the directed Fukaya category of the LG model and why we expect this to be mirror to the birational semi-orthogonal decomposition of the original toric stack X.

speaker: Ilia Zharkov
title: Tropical Pryms, conic bundles and cubic threefolds
abstract: I will discuss non-rationality of cubic threefolds from tropical perspective. This involves classification of rank 5 lattices.

speaker: Mikhail Mazin
title: Local Hilbert Schemes and Jacobi Factors of Plane Curve Singularities II
abstract: This is the third talk in the series. I will write down formulas relating cohomology of the local Hilbert schemes of a singularity to the cohomology of the Jacobi factor endowed with the perverse filtration and then show the combinatorial counterpart of this relation on the example of quasihomogeneous singularities.

speaker: Mikhail Mazin
title: Combinatorial models for the local Hilbert scheme and Jacobi factor in the quasihomogeneous case
abstract: In this talk I will discuss and compare combinatorial models for homology of the local Hilbert scheme and Jacobi factor of a quasihomogeneous plane curve singularity. I will also formulate some conjectures about these combinatorial models and their relation to the perverse filtration on the Jacobi factor.

speaker: Jason Lo
title: Stable complexes and Fourier-Mukai transforms
abstract: Fourier-Mukai transforms have been used to understand the relationships between various moduli spaces of sheaves, such as in the work of Bruzzo-Maciocia and Bridgeland-Maciocia. In this talk, I will give two examples - one on K3 surfaces and one on elliptic threefolds - where a moduli of complexes is mapped into a moduli of sheaves via a Fourier-Mukai transform.

speaker: Kevin Costello
title: Algebraic structures in perturbative quantum field theory
abstract: I'll discuss my work with Owen Gwilliam, where we develop an approach to perturbative quantum field theory which is similar to the deformation-quantization approach to quantum mechanics. From this point of view, the theory of renormalization provides a proof that we can deform a classical algebraic structure into a quantum one.

speaker: Kai Behrend
title: On the eigenvalue spectrum of the Inertia operator
abstract: We study the question whether the inertia operator on the Grothendieck module of algebraic stacks is diagonalizable. Answering this question may shed light on some of the mysterious operations defined by Joyce in his work on stack functions. This is joint work with Pooya Ronagh.

speaker: Eric Zaslow
title: Constructible Sheaves and Mirror Symmetry
abstract:
I will review some results relating the theory of constructible sheaves to the Fukaya category, and the relation to mirror symmetry for toric varieties. With this in hand, I will then discuss conjectural constructible models of the categories involved in mirror symmetry of Calabi-Yau manifolds at the large complex / large radius limit points.

speaker: Chit Ma
title: Fourier transforms in the SYZ program
abstract: Mirror symmetry is a duality between complex geometry and symplectic geometry. In this talk I will explain the Strominger-Yau-Zaslow proposal which explains mirror symmetry via Fourier type transformation along Lagrangian fibrations. I will also discuss recent progress on the SYZ proposal.

speaker: Rina Anno
title: Mukai-type flops via D-modules
abstract: This talk is based on a joint work in progress with Ivan Mirkovic. Flops are a special class of birational maps between algebraic varieties. It is expected that when two varieties are related by a flop, their derived categories of coherent sheaves are equivalent. However, it was shown by Namikawa in 2002 that even in the low-dimensional case of the so-called Mukai flop between two copies of $T^*P^2$ the functor immediately associated to the flop is not an equivalence, and while the equivalence still exists, it is given by a different functor. It turns out that if we switch to the world of D-modules then both of these functors can be explained quite naturally, and equivalences can be produced for a wide class of similar flops between $T^*X$, where $X$ are Grassmannians and other partial flag varieties.

speaker: Vivek Shende
title: Plane curve singularities, Hilbert schemes, HOMFLY homology, and Cherednik algebras
abstract: I will discuss a conjecture identifying the cohomology of certain nested Hilbert schemes of points on a plane curve singularity with the HOMFLY homology of the link of that singularity. The conjecture may be restated in terms of the cohomology of parabolic Hitchin fibers, in which form, and when restricted to toric singularities, it suggests the existence of the action of a rational Cherednik algebra on the HOMFLY homology of torus knots. As a consequence, the conjectures predict that the homology of (n,n+1) torus knots is described by formulas familiar from Haiman's study of diagonal harmonics, and the (n,mn+1) torus knots by known generalizations of these.

speaker: Lev Borisov
title: Vertex algebra approach to mirror symmetry
abstract: I will review the vertex algebra approach to mirror symmetry, including recent developments such as unification of Batyrev-Borisov and Berglund-Hubsch toric examples.

speaker: Lev Borisov
title: What is Mirror Symmetry in String Theory?
abstract: String theory attempts to describe the physical world by expressing fundamental forces and forms of matter in terms of tiny vibrating one-dimensional objects (strings) in place of usual points in space. While string theory is yet to be tested experimentally, it has considerable inner beauty and has spawned a number of fascinating mathematical developments. Mirror Symmetry is one such mathematical offshoot, and is the primary object of study at the M-center at Kansas State University. I will give an overview of the subject and its history for the general audience.

speaker: Diego Matessi
title: On Lagrangian spheres, sheaves and mirror symmetry of open Calabi-Yau's
abstract: I will describe a precise conjecture on the homological mirror symmetry of A_n singularities in dimension 3. To support this conjecture, I will discuss some results on the topology of Lagrangian sections and vanishing cycles via Lagrangian fibrations. Although the main motivation is to understand A_n singularities, the methods apply to more general open Calabi-Yau manifolds and seem to promise various generalizations. This is work in progress with Mark Gross.

speaker: Sheel Ganatra
title: Symplectic Cohomology and the Hochschild (co)homology of the Fukaya category
abstract: A Lefschetz fibration is a map from a symplectic manifold to a Riemann surface such that the fibers are symplectic submanifolds. In this talk I will give some constructions of Lefschetz fibrations and talk about some of their basic properties. This will include things like parallel transport, monodromy, vanishing cycles and matching cycles.

speaker: Ilia Itenberg
title: Lines on smooth quartic surfaces
abstract: It is a common understanding that, thanks to the global Torelli theorem and the surjectivity of the period map, any reasonable question concerning the topology and geometry of K3-surfaces can be reduced to a certain arithmetical problem. We apply this ideology to the study of the possible configurations of straight lines on a nonsingular quartic surface in ${\Bbb P}^3$. According to C. Segre, a nonsingular quartic in A ${\Bbb P}^3$ may contain at most 64 lines, and one explicit example of a surface with exactly 64 lines is known. The original proof, using classical algebraic geometry in the Italian school style, is quite complicated. We reprove Segre's result using the contemporary arithmetical approach. In addition, we prove that, up to projective equivalence, a nonsingular quartic with 64 lines is unique. Furthermore, we show that a real nonsingular quartic may contain at most 56 real line (Joint work with A. Degtyarev.)

speaker: Ivan Mirkovic
title: A geometric theory of modular representations of Lie algebras
abstract: This is a joint work with Roman Bezrukavnikov and Dmitriy Rumynin. The goal is to give a reasonable explanation of the new level of complexity that one encounters when one tries to rework known representation theories in the "modular context'', i.e., working over a field of positive characteristic p. At the first glance the modular versions are much more complicated due to amalgamation of random "accidents" -- the integers that happen to be divisible by p become zero in characteristic p. However, the final answer is simple: the effect of modular setting is a partial failure of the quantization of commutative geometry to noncommutative geometry. The new complexity is then found to correspond to the usual commutative geometry which has survived the quantization process. Once the problem has been reduced to commutative geometry, it is amenable to a rich world of algebro geometric machineries.

speaker: James Pascaleff
title: Some Aspects of Floer Theory on Log Calabi-Yau Surfaces
abstract: A Log Calabi-Yau surface is a pair consisting of a projective surface Y and an effective anticanonical divisor D. When D supports an ample class, the complement is naturally an exact symplectic manifold, and we will consider some aspects of its Floer theory, namely symplectic cohomology (generated by periodic orbits of a Hamiltonian), and Lagrangian intersection Floer cohomology. This study is motivated by mirror symmetry, and many of the geometric arguments are guided by the SYZ picture.

speaker: Ilia Itenberg
title: On real determinantal quartics
abstract: To four real symmetric 4 x 4 matrices $A_0$, $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$, one can associate a {\it determinantal s urface} in the three dimensional complex projective space ${\Bbb C}P^3$ (the set of points $(x_0 : x_1 : x_2 : x_3)$ in ${\Bbb C}P^3$ such that the determinant of the matrix $x_0 A_1 + x_1 A_1 + x_2 A_2 + x_3 A_3$ is zero) and a {\it spectrahedron} in the three dimensional real projectiv e space ${\Bbb R}P^3$ (the set of points $(x_0 : x_1 : x_2 : x_3)$ in ${\Bbb R}P^3$ such that the matrix $x_0 A_1 + x_1 A_1 + x_2 A_2 + x_3 A_3$ is semidefinite). In general, the determinantal surface considered has ten double points. We consider generic determinantal surfaces with non-e mpty spectrahedron and describe all possible arrangements of the ten nodes of such a surface. The proof is based on a study of period spaces of real K3-surfaces.

speaker: Grigory Mikhalkin
title: Classical Algebraic Geometry in the Tropical Limit
abstract: Complex numbers are key ingredient in the language of quantum mechanics. Even the motion of a particle is described through a change in its phase. In the same time in a whole range of actual problems (cf. e.g. celestial mechanics) there is little sense to use the full quantum mechanics machinery for description. The adequate description can be provided already by the classical tools. There is a somewhat similar situation in algebraic geometry. However here the term "classical" is reserved for more universal complex geometry. Algebraic geometry corresponding to the quasiclassical approximation is based on the so-called "tropical numbers" (named so after the Brazilian computer science school of Imre Simon) and is called "tropical geometry". As in quantum mechanics there is a correspondence principle between tropical and classical problems in algebraic geometry. In the talk we consider several examples of such correspondences.

speaker: Boris Khesin
title: Topological and Symplectic Hydrodynamics
abstract: Topological fluid dynamics studies topological features of flows with complicated trajectories and their applications to fluid motions. Its main ideas can be traced back to the seminal 1966 paper by V. Arnold on the Euler equation for an ideal fluid as the geodesic equation on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. In the lecture we survey various results related to Arnold's program in hydrodynamics and discuss recent results on invariants of ideal and symplectic fluid flows.

speaker: Mikhail Kapranov
title: Arakelov Coherent Sheaves and Their Hall Algebra
abstract: If X is a curve over a finite field, then the Hall algebra of coherent sheaves on X is an interesting quantum group-type object, related to quantum affine sl(2) (for X a projective line) and the Cherednik algebra (for X elliptic). The lecture will discuss the analogous algebra for the case when X is an arithmetic curve (spectrum of the ring of integers in a number field), compactified at infinity in the sense of Arakelov. Among other things, this leads to the concept of coherent sheaves on arithmetic curves with torsion at infinity, as well as to shuffle algebras based on Dedekind zeta functions.

speaker: Nikolai Reshetikhin
title: Quantum Field Theory: Are We There Yet?
abstract: Just as the development of quantum mechanics in 1920-1930 stimulated many branches of mathematics, attempts to construct quantum field theory gave boost to such areas as functional analysis, geometry and topology (gauge theories), representation theory of infinite-dimensional Lie algebras and related Hopf algebras (conformal and integrable field theories). And yet mathematically sound formulation of models in quantum field theory and their analysis remain a formidable mathematical problem. The lecture will start with a short historic overview. Then the concept of local quantum field theory will be outlined, followed by a discussion of perturbative versus non-perturbative quantum field theory and of successes and open problems. As an illustration of how naturally geometrical structures appear in quantum field theory, we will see that the locality of free scalar field naturally leads to Burghelea-Friedlander-Kappeler identities of Meyer-Vietoris type for determinants of Laplace operators.

speaker: Slava Kharlamov
title: First steps in real enumerative geometry
abstract: Surprisingly, in several real enumerative problems the number of real solutions happens to be comparable (for example, in logarithmic scale) with the number of complex ones. Currently, such a phenomenon is best studied in the case of interpolation of real points on a real rational surface by real rational curves. The key tool here is given by the Welschinger invariants (which can be seen as a real analogue of genus zero Gromov-Witten invariants). In this talk, based on joint works with I. Itenberg and E. Shustin, I will explain what Welschinger invariants look like in the case of surfaces, point certain modifications, and present some recursive formulas that allow to control Welschinger invariants in the case of Del Pezzo surfaces. Using this, I'll explain how to establish some basic properties of the invariants that imply, in particular, the abundance of real solutions.

speaker: Emanuel Diaconescu
title: Homfly polynomials in the stable pair theory of conifold
abstract: Hilbert schemes of points on plane curve singularities are related via wallcrossing to stable pair invariants of the resolved conifold. This construction places the conjecture of Oblomkov and Shende on Homfly polynomials in a Calabi-Yau threefold framework, leading to various generalizations.

speaker: Nick Sheridan
title: Homological Mirror Symmetry for a Calabi-Yau hypersurface in projective space
abstract: We prove homological mirror symmetry for a Calabi-Yau hypersurface in projective space. In the one-dimensional case, this is the elliptic curve, and our result is related to that of Polishchuk-Zaslow; in the two-dimensional case, it is the K3 quartic surface, and our result reproduces that of Seidel; and in the three-dimensional case, it is the quintic three-fold (also considered by Nohara-Ueda, using our work). After stating the result carefully, we will describe some of the techniques used in its proof. Namely, we will introduce equivariant versions of the affine and relative Fukaya categories, explain how they behave under ramified covers, and how to use a Morse-Bott model to make computations in them. We will go through the one-dimensional case with pictures. Finally, we will outline how to make computations in the derived category of coherent sheaves, via graded matrix factorizations.

speaker: Ron Donagi
title: Quantum Sheaf Cohomology
abstract: Quantum cohomology of a variety X is a refinement of its ordinary cohomology which captures very detailed information about numbers of curves in X. Combined with mirror symmetry, it has led to amazing advances in enumerative geometry. Now physicists tell us that there should exist a similar refinement, quantum sheaf cohomology, of the cohomology of a variety valued in a vector bundle E or in a more general coherent sheaf. This bundle needs to be "omalous" (not anomalous), which means that its first two Chern classes should match those of X. The usual (quantum) cohomology is recovered as the case that E is the tangent bundle of X. I will discuss recent progress on defining and calculating this quantum sheaf cohomology for toric varieties and hypersurfaces in them, as well as many open problems in this young field.

speaker: Valery Lunts
title: Motivic Measure
abstract: A motivic measure is a ring homomorphism from the Grothendieck ring of varieties to another commutative ring. One uses such homomorphisms to define Euler characteristic type of invariants of algebraic varieties. I will give a survey of known interesting motivic measures and also report on the work in progress where we construct some new ones.

speaker: Emanuele Macri
title: Bogomolov-type inequalities in higher dimension
abstract: In this seminar (based on joint work with A. Bayer, Y. Toda, and A. Bertram), we will present a conjectural approach to the construction of Bridgeland stability conditions on the derived category of a higher dimensional variety. The main ingredient is a generalization to complexes of the classical Bogomolov inequality for sheaves. We will also discuss an application of this inequality to the Fujita Conjecture for threefolds.

speaker: Dmitri Arinkin
title: Autoduality of Jacobians for singular curves
abstract: Let C be a (smooth projective algebraic) curve. It is well known that the Jacobian J of C is a principally polarized abelian variety. In other words, J is self-dual in the sense that J is identified with the space of topologically trivial line bundles on itself. Suppose now that C is singular. The Jacobian J of C parametrizes topologically trivial line bundles on C; it is an algebraic group which is no longer compact. By considering torsion-free sheaves instead of line bundles, one obtains a natural singular compactification J' of J. In this talk, I consider (projective) curves C with planar singularities. The main result is that J' is self-dual: J' is identified with a space of torsion-free sheaves on itself. This autoduality naturally fits into the framework of the geometric Langlands conjecture; I hope to sketch this relation in my talk.
